bib.title: A Neural Attention Model for Sentence Summarization

question: Can a fully data-driven neural model with a local attention encoder generate abstractive single-sentence summaries (headlines) at scale?
hypothesis: A neural language model conditioned on a soft-aligned attention encoder, trained end to end on millions of pairs, beats syntax-based and MT baselines.
contributions: Attention-Based Summarization (ABS): NNLM decoder plus attention-based encoder, trained jointly
Beam-search decoder and small set of extractive features tuned with MERT (ABS+)
Training on about 4 million Gigaword headline-sentence pairs
Gains over TOPIARY on DUC-2004 and over MOSES+ on Gigaword

method.summary: A feed-forward NNLM (context C=5) conditioned on an encoder (bag-of-words, convolutional TDNN, or attention-based) predicts each summary word; trained with minibatch SGD on NLL over Gigaword first-sentence/headline pairs. Decoding is beam search; ABS+ adds 5 log-linear features (unigram/bigram/trigram match, reordering) with weights tuned by MERT.

datasets.name: Annotated Gigaword (headline + first sentence)
datasets.size: roughly J = 4 million title-article pairs after filtering (from about 9.5 million articles); 119 million input tokens, 110K input word types, 31 million headline tokens, 69K headline types
datasets.split: validation set used for hyperparameters and perplexity (size not stated)
datasets.source: Graff et al. 2003; Napoles et al. 2012; Stanford CoreNLP tokenization
datasets.preprocessing: Filters: no common non-stop-words, byline or editing marks in title, question mark or colon in title. PTB tokenization, lower-casing, digits to #, word types seen fewer than 5 times to UNK. Articles from the DUC period removed. Average input 31.3 words, average title 8.3 words.

datasets.name: DUC-2004
datasets.size: 500 news articles, 4 human reference summaries each, capped at 75 bytes
datasets.split: evaluation only; only first sentence of article used
datasets.preprocessing: all system output cut off after 75 characters

datasets.name: DUC-2003
datasets.size: similarly sized to DUC-2004 (exact size not stated)
datasets.split: used for MERT tuning and for Table 3 ablations

datasets.name: Gigaword held-out test
datasets.preprocessing: systems tuned to produce output of average title length

models.name: ABS (attention encoder enc3 + NNLM)
models.architecture: feed-forward NNLM with attention-based bag-of-words style encoder
models.vocab: 110K input types, 69K headline types (types seen <5 times to UNK)

models.name: ABS+
models.architecture: ABS plus 5-feature log-linear rescoring with MERT-tuned weights alpha

models.name: MOSES+
models.architecture: phrase-based SMT trained on Gigaword, with deletion rules, infinite distortion limit, MERT tuned to 75-byte ROUGE

models.name: TOPIARY, PREFIX, COMPRESS, IR (BM25), W&L, REFERENCE

training.objective: negative log-likelihood of summaries given input, with gold contexts
training.lr_schedule: halve learning rate if validation log-likelihood does not improve for an epoch
training.regularisation: embedding tables renormalized after each epoch (Hinton et al. 2012)
training.compute: 1000 minibatches with D=200, H=400 take 160 seconds

other.MERT: Z-MERT (Zaidan 2009) on DUC-2003 data, weights alpha in R^5

inference.max_tokens: fixed output length N; DUC outputs cut at 75 bytes

parameters.alpha_features: 5: log p, unigram match, bigram match, trigram match, reordering indicator

metrics.name: ROUGE-1/2/L recall
metrics.definition: recall-oriented ROUGE (Lin 2004) with output cut at 75 bytes on DUC; Gigaword uses single reference

metrics.name: Perplexity
metrics.definition: language-model perplexity on Gigaword validation set, C=5

metrics.name: Ext. %
metrics.definition: percentage of summary tokens that also appear in the input

eval.protocol: single run; significance by default ROUGE confidence level; no human evaluation

availability.code: stated as to be openly available (Torch) with data pipeline

limits: Authors concede the model is far from human performance and reorders words in syntactically incorrect ways, giving wrong subjects and attachment errors (Section 8).
Output length is fixed and known in advance; only the first sentence of each article is used.
Feed-forward NNLM with a fixed context window; RNN decoder left to future work.
Only ROUGE is reported, no human evaluation; ROUGE rewards extractive features, which ABS+ exploits.
Beam size, GPU type, validation set size and seeds are not stated.
Superseded by RNN and Transformer seq2seq and pointer-generator summarizers.

terms.definition: a system is abstractive if it tries to find the optimal sequence from the set Y of all sentences of length N

lineage.work: Neural machine translation by jointly learning to align and translate
lineage.note: attention encoder modeled on Bahdanau et al.
